name: pdk-orchard-cluster-media-consistency
instr:
Our two OrchardCore hosts share one S3 media bucket, but editors can still see deleted images on the other host, a re-upload can show old bytes, and concurrent uploads to one name both claim success although one silently overwrites the other. Fix cluster consistency for S3-backed media in `/app/src` without changing the public media API.

`POST /api/media/Upload` must create an exact key only if absent across hosts: among eight concurrent uploads of one name with different bytes, exactly one succeeds, every loser reports the existing “already exists” error, and both hosts and S3 contain the winner's bytes. A prefix-sharing different key is not a collision. `POST /api/media/DeleteMedia` removes the file from both hosts' `/media/{path}` within 5 seconds; deleting then re-uploading the same name exposes the new bytes on both hosts within 5 seconds, even for equal-length content. A successful `POST /api/media/MoveMedia` removes the source and serves the destination on both hosts within 5 seconds; when a move races an upload to its destination, exactly one operation succeeds, the destination contains that operation's bytes on both hosts and in S3 when both requests finish, the source remains if the upload wins, and a successful move removes the source. If Redis is unavailable for 20 seconds during a delete and a move, these writes still succeed and the other host serves neither old path and serves the moved destination within 15 seconds of recovery. Restore publish and subscriptio
